Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

I first noticed $178.21 in the total field on a general studio page, which also lists other services, and thought for a moment that it might relate to our appointment. When I opened the individual payment notice, the line attached to Mara’s lesson showed $35.94. The bank notification also showed $35.94. I asked the studio to confirm which figure belonged to the booking, rather than assuming that the larger figure was an updated lesson price. The reply said, “For Mara’s appointment, the amount is $35.94; $178.21 is not the lesson charge.” That answer matches the payment notice and the calendar details.

She has been practicing the first part of “Ode to Joy” from a beginner book, but the email does not say that she must bring it or that it will be the lesson’s set piece. I put the book in her bag so it is available, while understanding that Jonah may choose a different starting exercise after they meet. We have not sent the studio a recording, and we have not asked for a particular teaching method. The note about the book is useful background about what Mara has tried at home, not a request to make the lesson focus on that tune. She can bring the book and let Jonah see it if there is time.

There is a check-in instruction in the email, but it is brief. It says to use the courtyard entrance and ask at the front desk for Room 2. I have not been to Cedar Room Music Studio before, so the entrance detail matters more to me than the street address alone. The email does not give a parking reservation, and I have not requested one. It says there is a bicycle rack in the courtyard, which may be useful if Mara and I cycle there, but it does not promise a space for a car. We have not decided whether to walk, cycle, or drive. I am keeping the arrival note with the appointment details so we do not mistakenly go to the street-facing door and have to look for another entrance at 5:30.

The studio’s email says that questions about the booking can be sent by replying to the confirmation. I asked about the amount and received the quoted answer above; I have not asked the studio to change the date, time, teacher, room, or lesson length. The confirmation remains for May 18 at 5:30 p.m. with Jonah Reed. It does not mention a second appointment, a recurring weekly slot, or a package of lessons, so I have not entered any follow-up dates in the calendar. The payment notice is for this booking only, and the separate larger figure remains excluded from the amount charged for Mara’s lesson.

Mara’s school pickup usually finishes shortly before the time we need to leave, and her music book is currently in the front pocket of her blue backpack. I will check that the book is still there before we go. The confirmation does not ask us to complete a placement form or bring any paperwork, and there is no note about a uniform or special equipment. Those details are separate from the appointment itself, but they are the practical things I need to remember when getting her ready.
